deck: This week’s signals highlight a surge in funding and strategic partnerships across the space sector.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured a $190 million Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding will bolster its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, which are increasingly critical as geopolitical tensions rise. With the DoD pulling through, the company is well-positioned to capitalize on defense contracts.
stories.soWhat: In a world where cash often trumps actual innovation, True Anomaly's funding reflects the defense sector's appetite for co-orbital capabilities.

stories.head: Ariane 6 preps for 36 Amazon Leo satellites
stories.body: The upcoming Ariane 6 launch is set to carry 36 Amazon Leo satellites, utilizing upgraded boosters to enhance payload capacity. This launch represents a significant step in Amazon's ambitions to dominate the broadband market. The stakes are high, as the success of this mission could redefine satellite internet services.
stories.soWhat: Amazon's satellite fleet could either be a game-changer or just another expensive lesson in space entrepreneurship.

stories.head: Palantir wins $480M extension on TITAN program
stories.body: Palantir Technologies has secured a $480 million extension on its TITAN ground station program, underscoring the company's persistent hold on government contracts. This extension is indicative of the defense sector's reliance on data analytics, especially as the military increasingly integrates AI into operations.
stories.soWhat: In government contracting, it seems the key to success is simply sticking around long enough to be indispensable.

watchlist.title: Potential IPOs on the horizon
watchlist.body: With the defense-tech IPO window cracking open, expect increased scrutiny on companies looking to go public.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser moves forward
watchlist.body: Having cleared its critical design review, the Dream Chaser DoD variant is one step closer to operational reality, but let's not hold our breath just yet.

watchlist.title: Ariane 6 launch date approaches
watchlist.body: As the Ariane 6 launch nears, all eyes will be on its success and what it means for future commercial satellite endeavors.

watchlist.title: Watch for defense funding shifts
watchlist.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion for space resilience suggests a growing emphasis on national security in space strategy.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
